# vMLX 1.6.58

This checkpoint improves remote API controls, tool-call continuation, SSD prefix lookup, and prefill lifecycle handling.

## Changes

- Remote Chat Completions and Responses sessions send protocol-specific reasoning controls and preserve tool-call IDs even when providers stream the ID separately from the function name and arguments. Remote throughput is labelled as an observed request-window rate, with counts accumulated across tool continuations.
- New Qwen Flash-Next desktop sessions start with MTP Off. Existing saved MTP choices and other families' defaults are preserved. When enabled, the selected depth remains a ceiling; switching decisions account for warmup and probing cost.
- SSD prefix lookup avoids redundant index scans and repeated key hashing. Supported hybrid checkpoints remain restorable, and each tool generation has its own durability boundary before continuation.
- Prefill releases completed chunk arrays promptly, reports completed work, and supports cancellation at worker-safe boundaries. Context and output admission use the loaded model's declared limits, without a family-wide 256K clamp.
- Ollama gateway media controls, reasoning effort, notices and typed errors are preserved. Malformed tool argument objects are rejected without invented replacement arguments. Partial Gemma channel markers are kept out of terminal content, and selected sessions survive stop/restart.

## Compatibility and limits

- MTP does not guarantee that every decoding window exceeds autoregressive speed. Experimental optimizations remain opt-in unless separately qualified.
- One-million-token inference is not certified by this release; a model's declared context configuration remains authoritative.
- GLM-5.3 mixed-state persistent SSD reuse is not supported. Its native-video quality and the proposed performance targets remain limitations.
- Independent external-provider generation and opaque Responses reasoning-history replay remain unqualified; provider capabilities differ.
- JANG tools remain at 2.5.47. This checkpoint does not change model weights or JANG quantization formats.

## Artifacts

Apple Silicon DMGs are provided separately for Sequoia and Tahoe. The wheel and source distribution are attached to the vMLX source release. Exact artifact hashes, source provenance and the JANG pin are recorded in `release-info.json`.
